rationale: Both candidates independently rediscover the substantive live issues (unpinned version=1 undermining train/rollout parity, missing kernel-load caching, FA3 gate admitting Blackwell, ~150 lines of duplicated Impl code, the residual varlen-None crash risk, and CI-lane selection problems), giving them similar core substance. Y edges ahead on recall by directly matching wtomin's inline ask for an is_cuda skipif/marker on the hardware test and touching the kernels version-pin question via pyproject.toml, both of which X misses entirely; X never engages the test-marker thread at all. Y's findings are also more rigorously grounded, quoting exact source lines as evidence for nearly every claim (including files outside the diff like layer.py and .buildkite configs), whereas X asserts suspiciously precise unverifiable specifics (exact commit SHAs, wall-clock benchmarks, 'kernels 0.16.0' despite the repo pinning <0.15.0) that read as plausible but harder to trust. X is slightly more polished and prescriptive in its fix suggestions, giving it a marginal actionability edge, but this doesn't offset Y's broader ground-truth coverage and stronger evidentiary grounding.
